labelVsPolicy.decision: A label change NEVER re-provisions the policy. update() accepts no label field; policyId is written only when explicitly passed.
labelVsPolicy.documentedBehaviour: Changing only the label (name / AgentRole / TeamMember.roleId) changes the display label and the bound role identity but leaves policyId and effectivePermission byte-identical. Changing capability requires an explicit PATCH policyId on the agent or PATCH /execution-policies/:policyId config.
labelVsPolicy.unitProof: update（PATCH /agents/:id）› update：不传 policyId → 不触碰原绑定，且改名（标签变更）不重配策略 — asserts executionPolicy.create/findUnique and agentRole.findUnique NOT called, result.policyId unchanged

liveProof.patch: PATCH /agents/a_0000000008 {name:'t4 renamed label', role:'tester'} -> 200; policyId still ep_0000000008; 'role' key silently stripped by whitelist pipe (role field null in response)
liveProof.comparison: effectivePermission.policyId same=true, tools equal=true, permission equal=true; policy row config unchanged=true, updatedAt unchanged=true

picker.payloadShape: { name, prompt?, persona?, agentKey, agentRoleId? } — NO `role` key, ever
picker.options: GET /agent-roles rows filtered to the create key set (product/project_manager/architect/developer/tester); value = AgentRole.id (ar_ prefix); no label fallback (a fallback value would silently produce a skeleton)

whitelistStripDefectGuard.statement: The global ValidationPipe (whitelist:true) silently strips unknown DTO fields. If the picker still posted `role` after its removal from the DTO, every new agent would silently fall back to the skeleton.
whitelistStripDefectGuard.unitGuard: agents.controller.spec.ts › DTO 校验: runs the real ValidationPipe shape over create/update/clone DTOs and asserts agentRoleId survives while a stale `role` key is stripped (hasOwnProperty false)
whitelistStripDefectGuard.liveGuard: legacy-role-only POST /agents {role:'developer'} (no agentRoleId) → 201 with tools#=0, bash=deny (skeleton) — the old wire is verified DEAD end-to-end, not assumed
